geography.name: Location
geography.short_description: Identifies the state or school district a row describes.
geography.long_description: In data_state.csv.gz this is a FIPS code: "00" for national, otherwise a 2-digit state FIPS, including 11 for DC and 72 for Puerto Rico. In data_lea.csv.gz it is instead a 7-digit NCES LEAID identifying a school district, which is not a FIPS code; the containing state's FIPS is in the separate `state` column and is also the LEAID's first two digits. Together with `time` this is the primary key of each file.

geography_name.name: Location name
geography_name.short_description: Name of the state or school district.
geography_name.long_description: Name as published by NCES, with the trailing state name and postal abbreviation stripped, so "A-C Central Community Unit School District 262, Illinois, IL" becomes "A-C Central Community Unit School District 262". Names are refreshed with each vintage and are not stable across vintages; join on `geography` rather than on the name.

state.name: State
state.short_description: FIPS code of the state containing the school district.
state.long_description: 2-digit state FIPS code, which is also the first two digits of the LEAID. Present in data_lea.csv.gz only, where it is the join key to state-level data, since `geography` there holds an LEAID rather than a FIPS code. Covers 52 values: the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico.

lea_type.name: District type
lea_type.short_description: Whether the district is elementary, secondary or unified.
lea_type.long_description: The three types are separate geographic layers that overlap one another: in dual-district states an elementary and a secondary district cover the same ground. Rows must therefore not be summed across types, and data_state.csv.gz should be used for totals. Present in data_lea.csv.gz only. In the 2019-2023 vintage there are 10,878 unified, 1,957 elementary and 480 secondary districts.

time.name: Time
time.short_description: Last day of the final year of the ACS five-year period.
time.long_description: Written as YYYY-12-31, so the 2019-2023 estimates carry 2023-12-31. This follows the repository convention of dating annual data to the end of its year, but note that each value summarises five years of sample, not the one year named.

period.name: ACS period
period.short_description: The five-year span the estimates cover, as ACS publishes it.
period.long_description: For example "2019-2023". Kept alongside `time` because it is the label NCES and the Census Bureau use, and because it makes the five-year averaging explicit. Consecutive periods share four years of sample, so year-over-year differences are heavily autocorrelated and are not annual change. Fifteen periods are published, from 2005-2009 to 2019-2023.

nces_pop_total{variant}.short_description: Total population of the state or school district.
nces_pop_total{variant}.long_description: Total population, from ACS table B01003.{variant.note}

_moe.note: This column is the 90 percent margin of error of the estimate, and is empty far more often than the other margins here. ACS publishes "*****" instead of a margin of error wherever a population total is controlled to an independent estimate rather than sampled, which makes its sampling error zero by construction. That is true of every national and state row, so the column is entirely empty in data_state.csv.gz, and of districts coextensive with a controlled geography, which is why the largest districts (New York City, Puerto Rico) are empty too. Elsewhere in data_lea.csv.gz it is populated for 175,676 of 202,075 rows: the median district margin is 344 people, or about 6 percent of the estimate. The 2005-2009 vintage publishes no margins of error at all.

Districts where the median falls outside the published income brackets are left missing.{variant.note}

nces_median_household_income_bound.long_name: Whether the median household income fell outside the published brackets
nces_median_household_income_bound.short_description: Says whether the median household income is a usable number, or known only to be above or below the published range.
nces_median_household_income_bound.long_description: "within" where nces_median_household_income holds a usable value; "top" where ACS reported the median as "$250,000+"; "bottom" where it reported "$2,500-"; and empty where the median is missing for some other reason. For "top" and "bottom" the estimate itself is NA, because the true median is known only to lie beyond the bracket: at least $250,000, or at most $2,500. Use this column to tell a genuinely missing median apart from a very high or very low one, and to substitute the bracket bound if your analysis needs a number. Top-coded rows are rare but growing as incomes rise, from 2 districts in the 2006-2010 vintage to 37 in 2019-2023; bottom-coded rows never exceed 5.
nces_median_household_income_bound.statement: The median household income in {location} was {value} the published range.

nces_acs_ed.name: NCES ACS-ED Tables
nces_acs_ed.organization: National Center for Education Statistics, Education Demographic and Geographic Estimates (EDGE) program
nces_acs_ed.description: The EDGE program has the Census Bureau retabulate American Community Survey five-year period estimates onto school district boundaries, producing social, economic and housing indicators for school-age children and their families at national, state and school district level. Fifteen vintages are published, from 2005-2009 through 2019-2023, each covering roughly 13,400 elementary, secondary and unified districts alongside the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico. Because these are five-year survey averages for small areas, district-level margins of error are often large relative to the estimates and consecutive vintages share four years of sample, so year-over-year changes are heavily autocorrelated and should not be read as annual change. District boundaries are refreshed each year, so a district's geography is not necessarily constant across vintages. This source carries the survey-based measures of high school completion and dropout; the Adjusted Cohort Graduation Rate, which follows a single cohort to graduation and is reported by school rather than by residence, comes from the separate NCES EDFacts and Common Core of Data collections and is not part of these tables.
nces_acs_ed.restrictions: Public domain. NCES and Census Bureau data are generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

_catalog.summary: The ACS-ED tables describe children and families in every U.S. school district, covering school enrollment, child poverty, language, health insurance and high school completion.
